rdf:Description.dc:title: Woodrow Wilson's Sheep
rdf:Description.dc:description: During World War I, President Woodrow Wilson had flocks of sheep on the White House lawn. Although previous presidents had kept farm animals as pets, these sheep were part of a Presidential initiative to support the war effort. The sheep grazed on lawns as a way of lowering groundskeeping costs. When the sheep were sheared, their wool was auctioned off to help raise money for the Red Cross, totaling $52,823 by the end of the war.
rdf:Description.dc:source: National Archives, via Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library. View original.
